3. Environmental Effects, 100-year Flood Plain
The negative impacts brought about as a result of the project being within a 100 year unprotected flood plain will remain latent until the next flood in the area. Flood plain management measures, carried out under the project, will undoubtedly reduce the impact on the project area in future flooding situations; however, with regard to existing properties in the area, the effects of future flooding will probably not be much different than that experienced during past flooding. Most of these properties do not fall under the requirements of the proposed flood plain ordinance for the area. Aside from the fact that valuable natural resources and human life may be lost in future flooding, Federally sponsored flood insurance will be available to residents of the 100 year flood plain to compensate for property loss. The city of Harrisburg has been made eligible under the emergency program; therefore the residents of the area may apply for coverage.
The Flood Insurance Act of 1968, as amended, provides for Federal assistance in the form of guarantees to commercial insurance companies, who then issue flood insurance policies to individuals or small businesses, through the customer's insurance agent. The insuree's municipality must have applied to the Federal Insurance Administration for blanket insurance coverage, and must have been accepted for this coverage. Flood insurance is issued at low rates but with limited coverage, to individuals and to commercial enterprises.
Single dwellings may be insured to a value of $17,500; all other structures may be insured to $30,000. Contents coverage is available at subsidized rates in amounts up to $5,000 per unit and may be purchased by either the owner or the tenant. Pending legislation in the Congress would double these amounts.
The Small Business Administration requires most recepients of disaster relief loans to obtain flood insurance when available, much in the same way mortgage lenders require fire and extended coverage insurance on conventional loans. Therefore, many of the project residents will be required to obtain this insurance—many others will not.
Flood insurance will not compensate the environment for its loss during future flooding, but it will compensate those affected by the flood. This tends to make the reinvestment of private public funds in the project area slightly more acceptable.
